summary.leadingMessage: Revenue demand exists, but too many lanes still lose trust and recoverable value to control gaps, reporting fragmentation, and instrumentation drift.

items.boardQuestion: Where is AI demand converting into demos and policy narratives without equally strong attribution and commercial control proof?
items.currentPosture: The lane is commercially promising, but revenue proof still drifts between policy wins, partner influence, and actual closed-booking evidence.
items.breakageNarrative: AI demand is real, but attribution drift is still obscuring which control-led motions actually create revenue.
items.operatingReality: The story is strong, though too many wins still rely on inferred influence instead of a tighter revenue evidence chain.
items.riskHeadline: Board confidence is getting ahead of booking evidence because attribution still forks too easily across the AI lane.
items.breakageSignal: Executive briefings, policy packets, and operator surfaces point to traction, but pipeline evidence still lands in too many parallel systems.
items.blockingIssue: One commercial outcome still has to be reconciled across CRM notes, board memos, and platform narratives.
opportunityMoves: tie board memos to CRM proof
items.headline: AI governance has demand, but revenue proof still drifts.
items.narrative: This lane does not need more visibility; it needs tighter booking evidence tied back to the exact controls and products that moved the deal.
items.nextMove: Standardize one sourced-versus-influenced evidence packet for every AI governance win above the board-review threshold.

breakageAssessment.message: Revenue-control breakage is visible and should be tightened before it compounds.

reconciliationAssessment.message: Reconciliation work is rising and should be simplified.

instrumentationAssessment.message: Instrumentation gaps are visible and should be narrowed.

latencyAssessment.message: Reporting latency is slowing confidence and should be reduced.

controlAssessment.message: Control gaps are visible and should be tightened.

items.boardQuestion: Where are enterprise deals slowing because procurement friction is visible but its pipeline impact still is not measured tightly enough?
items.currentPosture: The trust lane is useful, but revenue controls still understate how much procurement delays are affecting close timing.
items.breakageNarrative: Procurement demand is measurable, but the pipeline blind spot is still too wide between trust effort and booked revenue.
items.operatingReality: The team is shipping answer packs and evidence rooms, but conversion drag still hides inside cycle-time variance rather than one crisp loss signal.
items.riskHeadline: Deals are getting delayed by procurement pressure without one consistent way to quantify the revenue exposure.
items.breakageSignal: Commercial teams can feel the drag, but the revenue system still does not tag proof-room effort, questionnaire burden, and close-delay outcomes in one place.
items.blockingIssue: Trust work is helping, but not all related revenue events are coded consistently enough to make the savings and acceleration story board-ready.
opportunityMoves: tie diligence effort to close timing
items.headline: Procurement is helping, but its revenue drag is still under-instrumented.
items.narrative: The next gain here comes from tighter instrumentation, not more generic trust copy.
items.nextMove: Add one canonical delay-and-reuse tagging model so procurement effort can be measured directly against revenue timing.

items.boardQuestion: Which regulated lane is commercially credible, but still too fragmented to report revenue readiness cleanly?
items.currentPosture: The lane is serious and differentiated, but commercial reporting still splits between quality-proof narratives and actual opportunity progression.
items.breakageNarrative: Biotech is strategically strong, though reporting fragmentation keeps weakening the commercial story.
items.operatingReality: There is real value here, but the evidence lives across too many adjacent rooms for clean board-facing revenue reporting.
items.riskHeadline: Leaders can see the regulated proof, but not always the clean revenue-throughline from evidence surface to booked opportunity.
items.breakageSignal: Quality, CAPA, specimen, and GxP work all look strong independently, yet still report through too many adjacent narratives.
items.blockingIssue: The lane needs one tighter commercialization rollup instead of four separate proof surfaces that require manual synthesis.
opportunityMoves: tie proof surfaces to one commercial readiness score
items.headline: Biotech is valuable, but still too reporting-fragmented.
items.narrative: This lane needs one standardized commercialization view that ties regulated proof to pipeline readiness without manual stitching.
items.nextMove: Publish one commercialization rollup for the biotech cluster and make it the only board-facing reporting packet.

items.boardQuestion: Where are control failures, reserve logic, or reconciliation gaps still leaking value out of an otherwise strong FinTech lane?
items.currentPosture: The category is commercially attractive, but payment and merchant-control breakage still distorts the economics.
items.breakageNarrative: FinTech is strong on demand, but payment leakage is still too high for clean board confidence.
items.operatingReality: Useful surfaces exist, though control breakage still shows up as reserve pressure, payout delay, and mismatched reconciliation narratives.
items.riskHeadline: The lane is winning attention, but control failures are still leaking money and trust.
items.breakageSignal: Merchant review, reconciliation, and treasury logic do not yet reconcile into one clean revenue protection packet.
items.blockingIssue: One control failure still creates too many downstream mismatches between payout, finance, and risk reporting.
items.headline: FinTech has pull, but control failure is still leaking money.
items.narrative: This lane needs tighter containment and revenue-protection reporting before the board should underwrite heavier expansion.
items.nextMove: Create one canonical exception taxonomy that connects merchant risk, payment reconciliation, and treasury outcomes.

breakageAssessment.message: Breakage is high enough to distort board confidence, reporting, or recovery logic.

reconciliationAssessment.message: Too much reconciliation work is leaking time and trust.

instrumentationAssessment.message: Instrumentation gaps are visible and should be narrowed.

latencyAssessment.message: Reporting latency is high enough to damage the revenue story.

controlAssessment.message: Control gaps are materially weakening the revenue and diligence posture.

items.boardQuestion: Which reusable lane still has demand, but forecasts too optimistically because stewardship and reporting do not reconcile tightly enough?
items.currentPosture: The lane has clear operator value, but commercial forecasting is still looser than the board story implies.
items.breakageNarrative: Nonprofit work is reusable, though forecast mismatch still blurs the revenue and renewal story.
items.operatingReality: The surfaces help, but reporting, stewardship, and outcome proof still do not collapse into one clean commercial narrative.
items.riskHeadline: The lane can look healthier than it is because forecast confidence is still built on fragmented signals.
items.breakageSignal: Grant evidence, donor stewardship, and outcomes work all point in the same direction, but not through one standardized forecast model.
items.blockingIssue: The current motion still needs one cleaner tie between operator demand, renewal probability, and realized revenue timing.
opportunityMoves: align stewardship signals with revenue timing
items.headline: Nonprofit is useful, but forecast confidence is still too soft.
items.narrative: The lane should stay active, but it needs a tighter forecast model tied to the real stewardship and evidence cycle.
items.nextMove: Use one renewal-confidence rollup across grants, stewardship, and outcomes instead of separate forecast assumptions.

items.boardQuestion: Which strategically interesting lane is still too thin on control proof to support bigger revenue assumptions?

items.breakageNarrative: Robotics can widen the story, though control gaps still make its revenue assumptions fragile.

items.riskHeadline: The board can see the vision, but not yet enough control proof to trust the revenue case fully.
items.breakageSignal: Override, fleet, and sensor narratives point to value, but the commercial controls behind them still need a tighter packet.
items.blockingIssue: The lane still needs one stronger evidence path between technical range and board-safe revenue confidence.
opportunityMoves: bundle override evidence into one commercial packet
items.headline: Robotics expands the story, but still needs stronger control proof.
items.narrative: This lane is strategically useful, but it should stay commercial-light until the control packet gets stronger and easier to trust.
items.nextMove: Build one board-safe control packet that ties override readiness, sensor health, and fleet exception evidence to a narrower revenue claim.
